title: Возвращение Баринова на кухню  (Barinov Returns to the Kitchen)

segments.t: Gathering the cooks in the kitchen, Lyova announces that Viktor Petrovich will be away recovering for another two weeks. As Senya jokes about the boss slacking off to drink beer, Chef Barinov himself steps out from hiding and scolds the laughing crew.
Виктора Петровича не будет еще две недели.
Он же целый месяц не работает.
Что бы я без тебя делал?
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
'May I have your attention for a minute.' Pointing out that may he has Ilya's attention for a minute gives Ilya a sobering reality check.
'Anyway, here is the news.' Vika explains that anyway here is the news, keeping her voice calm and direct.
Виктора Петровича не будет еще две недели.
'Viktor Petrovich will be away for another two weeks.' Realizing that Viktor Petrovich will be away for another two weeks changes how Ilya handles the situation.
Он же целый месяц не работает.
'He has not worked for a whole month already.' Having not worked for a whole month already is how Barinov lays out the situation for Ilya.
'And now he has gone off to drink beer on vacation.' Even though he has gone off to drink beer on vacation, Vika keeps a steady face in front of Barinov.

'How can you not be ashamed of yourself?' Here wondering how Barinov not be ashamed of themselves can shows Ilya looking for the real truth. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.

'How could we possibly talk like that?' By asking how they possibly talk like could, Barinov presses Ilya for a straight answer. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
'He is sick and he needs medical treatment.' Once he is sick and he needs medical treatment, Vika can finally tell Barinov what she means.

'What are you all laughing at?' Asking what Barinov all laughing is is how Ilya puts Barinov on the spot. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
Что бы я без тебя делал?

'What would I ever do without you?' Here asking what he ever do without Ilya would shows Barinov looking for the real truth. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
'Alright, alright, alright.' Between the boss and the work, Vika gives Barinov a quick, grounded response.
'That is enough.' Mentioning that that is enough moves the talk in a new direction.

'So how are you doing in here?' Wondering how Ilya doing in here is is how Barinov puts Ilya on the spot. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects. Let's hear the full exchange one more time at natural speed.
Виктора Петровича не будет еще две недели.
Он же целый месяц не работает.
Что бы я без тебя делал?
That wraps up this scene as lyova announces that Chef Barinov will be away for two more weeks, only for Barinov himself to step out and catch Senya joking about him drinking beer. See you next time!
